commands.description: LinkedIn account connection management.
List connected LinkedIn accounts.

args.name: external-id
args.description: Only accounts whose external_id (your own end-user id, set on link) equals this value exactly.

commands.description: Get a connected LinkedIn account: its status (active, reconnect_needed, restricted, connecting or disconnected) and its per-action quotas. --verbose adds cached profile fields, which may be null.

args.name: account-id
args.description: Account id (acc_...).

commands.description: List the workspace's live seats and whether each is free or bound to an account. A seat with occupied:false (free) is a seat_id `curviate account link --seat-id` accepts right now. Not paginated (bounded by purchased seats), --all is not supported. An empty result can mean the workspace has no seats, or that billing needs attention.

Connect a LinkedIn account to an empty seat. If LinkedIn requires verification you'll be prompted for the code interactively. Given --auth-method and its credentials, a non-interactive shell exits 12 at that step and you finish with `curviate account checkpoint solve <account_id> --code`.

args.name: seat-id
args.description: Empty seat to bind the account to, listed by `curviate account seats` (a free seat there is one this call accepts right now). Omit it and the only free seat is used; with zero or several free the command says so and connects nothing. Required with --preview (which calls nothing) and with --account-id (a reconnect keeps the seat that account already holds).

args.name: auth-method
args.description: Authentication method: credentials | cookie.

args.name: email
args.description: LinkedIn email (credentials method).

args.name: password
args.description: LinkedIn password (credentials method). Note: a value on the command line is visible to other processes via `ps` and saved in shell history; prefer `--password-stdin` or the CURVIATE_LINKEDIN_PASSWORD env var.

args.name: password-stdin
args.description: Read the LinkedIn password from stdin (one line, trimmed).

args.name: li-at
args.description: LinkedIn session cookie li_at (cookie method). Note: a value on the command line is visible to other processes via `ps` and saved in shell history; prefer `--li-at-stdin` or the CURVIATE_LINKEDIN_LI_AT env var.

args.name: li-at-stdin
args.description: Read the li_at session cookie from stdin (one line, trimmed).

args.name: li-a
args.description: Optional premium session cookie li_a (cookie method). Note: a value on the command line is visible to other processes via `ps` and saved in shell history; prefer the CURVIATE_LINKEDIN_LI_A env var.

args.name: country
args.description: Where LinkedIn sees this account connecting from: a two-letter ISO 3166-1 country code (e.g. US, DE; case-insensitive), the country its owner normally signs in from. A new connect needs exactly one of --country, --ip or --proxy-host. Strict: the connect fails rather than use another country, unless --allow-country-fallback.

args.name: ip
args.description: A public IPv4 address whose country becomes the connection location (strict, like --country). An alternative to --country.

args.name: allow-country-fallback
args.description: With --country or --ip: allow a connection from another country when none is free in the chosen one. Without it the connect is strict and fails instead.

args.name: proxy-protocol
args.description: Proxy protocol: http | https | socks5 | socks4.

args.name: proxy-host
args.description: Your own proxy's host or IP. Your proxy decides where LinkedIn sees the account connecting from, so --country, --ip and --allow-country-fallback are not accepted with it.

args.name: proxy-port
args.description: Proxy port.

args.name: proxy-username
args.description: Proxy auth username.

args.name: proxy-password
args.description: Proxy auth password. Note: a value on the command line is visible to other processes via `ps` and saved in shell history; prefer the CURVIATE_PROXY_PASSWORD env var.

args.name: user-agent
args.description: Browser User-Agent to pin for this account. Required with --auth-method cookie: a session cookie only works paired with the User-Agent of the browser it was copied from, and the command exits 2 without it. Optional with --auth-method credentials, where it is still pinned for the account when given.

args.name: recruiter-contract-id
args.description: Recruiter contract to bind to. Only meaningful when the LinkedIn account holds a Recruiter subscription.

args.name: linkedin-premium
args.description: Narrow this connection to one LinkedIn premium surface: sales_navigator | recruiter. Omit it and the connect asks for every product and LinkedIn activates what the account holds. Applies to THIS call only and is never remembered, so restate it on every connect and reconnect where Recruiter must win.

args.name: products
args.description: Comma-separated premium products to ask for: sales_navigator, recruiter. Omit to ask for both (--linkedin-premium still narrows). Classic LinkedIn and company pages are always included.

args.name: external-id
args.description: Your own id for this account's end user (1-255 chars, not unique). Returned on the account and every account webhook; filter with `curviate account list --external-id`. Use an opaque id, not an email.

args.name: timezone
args.description: IANA time zone for the account, e.g. Europe/Berlin. A UTC offset is refused.

args.name: account-id
args.description: Existing account id (acc_...) to re-authenticate IN PLACE. Passing it makes this an in-place reconnect of that account. Omit to connect a NEW account into --seat-id.

args.name: no-interactive
args.description: Never prompt for a checkpoint code. On a checkpoint, always render the envelope and exit 12, even on a TTY.

examples: curviate account link --auth-method credentials --email jane@example.com --password-stdin --country US
curviate account link --auth-method credentials --email jane@example.com --password-stdin --account-id acc_YOUR_ACCOUNT_ID --seat-id SEAT_ID
requires: Exactly one of --country, --ip or --proxy-host on a new connect; a reconnect (--account-id) may omit it to keep the account's location.
--seat-id with --preview or --account-id, and when zero or several seats are free.
--password-stdin only with --auth-method credentials; --li-at-stdin only with --auth-method cookie.

commands.description: In-progress connect operations (poll for completion).

Poll the status of an in-progress connect (auth intent) for completion. Without --wait: a single poll. The JSON `status` field (pending | resolved | expired | failed) tells you what to do next. With --wait: block on the same adaptive cadence as `curviate account link` until a terminal state.

args.description: Wait-loop timeout in milliseconds (requires --wait; default: time remaining to the session's expiry). Note the unit: this is milliseconds.

args.name: session
args.description: The account's acc_... id, returned by `curviate account link` or a checkpoint response.

args.name: wait
args.description: Poll on an adaptive cadence (1000ms, then 1500ms for 30s, then 3000ms) until a terminal state, instead of a single poll.

args.name: account-id
args.description: Account id (acc_...).

On an account using your own proxy, pass --clear-proxy with it.

args.name: allow-country-fallback

args.name: clear-proxy
args.description: Stop using your own proxy and return to a managed location. Requires --country. Mutually exclusive with --proxy-host.

args.name: proxy-protocol
args.description: Proxy protocol: http | https | socks5 | socks4.

args.name: proxy-host
args.description: Your own proxy's host or IP. Not accepted with --country.

args.name: proxy-username

args.name: proxy-password

commands.description: Motions: one Sequence run for the Contacts of your Team's Contact lists, from its sending Accounts, paced on a schedule. Create and edit drafts, preview, start, pause, resume, archive, add or remove Contacts; lint a Sequence and write a template offline. Your Team's data: every role reads; writes need motion-send on each sending Account, and Motions need the Automate plan.

List your Team's Motions, most recently updated first (--sort activity: latest activity first, `last_activity_at`). Items carry no Sequence: read one with `curviate motion get <motion_id>`. A cursor belongs to its sort.

args.name: accounts
args.description: Only Motions sending from one of these Accounts: a comma list of ids (acc_...). --account a,b is accepted as the same filter.

args.name: sort
args.description: updated (default) or activity.

args.name: status
args.description: Comma list of draft, scheduled, active, paused, completed, archived. Default: all but archived.

commands.description: One Motion with its current Sequence and lint warnings. With --version, that Sequence version instead, and how many Enrollments still run on it.

args.name: id
args.description: Motion id (mot_...).

args.name: version
args.description: A Sequence version number (1 or more).

output: The full Motion, pasteable: `curviate motion create --file -` and `curviate motion update <motion_id> --file -` accept it as is, dropping the keys Curviate sets.

commands.description: Create a Motion from a Motion file, always as a draft: nothing runs until `curviate motion start`. The file is checked before anything is sent, its Sequence as `curviate motion lint` checks it. Needs Automate.

args.name: file
args.description: The Motion file: a path, or - to read it from stdin. `curviate motion get` output is accepted as is.

rules.changes: Creates a draft Motion. No Contact is enrolled and nothing reaches LinkedIn until it is started.
rules.visible_to: Your Team.
rules.retry: A retry creates a second draft: list with `curviate motion list --status draft` first.
rules.undo: `curviate motion delete <motion_id>` deletes a draft.

errors.SEQUENCE_INVALID: the Sequence breaks a rule; every error is listed, one line each, as `curviate motion lint` prints them.
errors.INSUFFICIENT_ROLE: your role cannot send from a sending Account of this Motion.
errors.ACCOUNT_NOT_SHARED: a sending Account is not shared with you.

commands.description: Change a Motion from a Motion file: objects (schedule, settings) merge by key, arrays and the Sequence replace whole, null clears. After start, a structural Sequence change makes a new version; running Enrollments keep theirs. With --if-revision the save is refused when someone saved the Sequence since. Needs Automate.

args.name: id
args.description: Motion id (mot_...).

args.name: file
args.description: The Motion file: a path, or - to read it from stdin. `curviate motion get` output is accepted as is.

args.name: if-revision
args.description: The sequence_revision you read (`curviate motion get`). The save is refused with SEQUENCE_CONFLICT when the stored Sequence moved past it. Omitted: the last save wins.

rules.changes: Changes the Motion. A running Motion picks the change up at each Enrollment's next Step.
rules.visible_to: Your Team, and the Contacts its next Steps reach.
rules.retry: Safe: the same file sends the same change. Without --if-revision the last save wins.
rules.undo: Send the previous file again (`curviate motion get <motion_id> --version <n>` reads an earlier Sequence).

errors.SEQUENCE_INVALID: the Sequence breaks a rule; every error is listed, one line each, as `curviate motion lint` prints them.
errors.SEQUENCE_CONFLICT: with --if-revision: someone saved the Sequence since that revision; the message names the newer revision and who saved it.
errors.MOTION_STATUS_CONFLICT: an archived Motion, or one past its end, cannot change.
errors.INSUFFICIENT_ROLE: your role cannot send from a sending Account of this Motion.
errors.ACCOUNT_NOT_SHARED: a sending Account is not shared with you.

commands.description: Start a draft: scheduled when its start time is ahead, else active. Freezes Sequence version 1. A Motion missing what it needs is refused with every gap listed. Needs Automate.

args.name: id
args.description: Motion id (mot_...).

rules.changes: The Motion starts enrolling its Contacts and running its Steps from its sending Accounts, paced on its schedule.
rules.visible_to: The Contacts each Step reaches on LinkedIn.
rules.retry: A retry on a started Motion answers MOTION_STATUS_CONFLICT; nothing runs twice.
rules.undo: `curviate motion pause <motion_id>` stops new Steps; what was sent stays sent.
rules.blast_radius: Every Contact of its Contact lists, from every sending Account, each Step spending that Account's budgets (`curviate account get <account_id>`).

errors.MOTION_NOT_STARTABLE: a gap stops it (Contact list, sending Account, Sequence); each is listed.
errors.INSUFFICIENT_ROLE: your role cannot send from a sending Account of this Motion.
errors.ACCOUNT_NOT_SHARED: a sending Account is not shared with you.

args.name: id
args.description: Motion id (mot_...).

rules.visible_to: Your Team.
rules.retry: Safe: a paused Motion answers MOTION_STATUS_CONFLICT.
rules.undo: `curviate motion resume <motion_id>`.

errors.MOTION_STATUS_CONFLICT: only an active or scheduled Motion pauses.
errors.INSUFFICIENT_ROLE: your role cannot send from a sending Account of this Motion.
errors.ACCOUNT_NOT_SHARED: a sending Account is not shared with you.

commands.description: Resume a paused Motion. Runs the start checks again. Needs Automate.

rules.undo: `curviate motion pause <motion_id>`; what was sent stays sent.
rules.blast_radius: Every open Enrollment of the Motion.

errors.MOTION_NOT_STARTABLE: a gap stops it; each is listed.
errors.INSUFFICIENT_ROLE: your role cannot send from a sending Account of this Motion.
errors.ACCOUNT_NOT_SHARED: a sending Account is not shared with you.

errors.INSUFFICIENT_ROLE: your role cannot send from a sending Account of this Motion.
errors.ACCOUNT_NOT_SHARED: a sending Account is not shared with you.

commands.description: Store a Draft. Every part is optional. With --schedule-at (and an account and text) Curviate publishes it at that time. args.name: account
args.description: Account the Draft publishes as (acc_...). Never defaulted: omit it for a Draft with no account yet.

args.description: Post text (up to 3000 characters). Pass - to read from stdin.

args.description: Publish at this time: ISO 8601 with an offset (e.g. 2026-10-12T09:00:00+02:00), passed through unchanged. A time in the future, not too close to another scheduled Draft on the same account (SCHEDULE_CONFLICT). Needs an account and text.

args.name: attach
args.description: File to attach, repeatable; keeps the order given. Several images (JPEG, PNG, GIF, WEBP), or one MP4 video, or one PDF, never mixed. A file over its size limit is refused.
